dfg-nok.title: Development of complex societies in sub-Saharan Africa: The Nigerian Nok Culture (project results)
dfg-nok.author: Goethe University Frankfurt, Nok project led by Peter Breunig; summary on the DFG GEPRIS project page
dfg-nok.kind: research project summary (primary for the project's own findings)
dfg-nok.rights: Facts and dates cited; no text, images or maps reproduced.
dfg-nok.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Phases 1500-900 BC, 900-400 BC, 400 BC to the turn of the era; almost 500 sites, 84 excavations, 270 radiocarbon dates; iron in the later part of phase 2.

scientia-breunig.title: Professor Peter Breunig: The Significance of Nok Culture Sculptures in Nigerian Prehistory
scientia-breunig.author: Scientia (science communication article about Breunig's research)
scientia-breunig.rights: CC BY 4.0 (stated on the page). Facts cited only.
scientia-breunig.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Start about 1500 BCE; terracottas from the 9th century BCE; sculpture production falls off around 400 BCE; Pangwari and Ifana named.

antiquity-kagarko.title: Exploring the Nok enigma
antiquity-kagarko.author: Nicole Rupp, Peter Breunig and Stefanie Kahlheber, Antiquity Project Gallery 82 (316)
antiquity-kagarko.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Janruwa, Janjala and Akura sites near Kagarko, about 1 km apart; Taruga named as the source of iron smelting evidence.

wiki-nok.title: Nok culture (Wikipedia)
wiki-nok.author: Wikipedia contributors; the facts used cite Shaw 1981 (Scientific American) and Fagg 1969 (World Archaeology)
wiki-nok.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-nok.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-nok.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. First terracotta found near Nok village in 1928 in a tin mine; 1943 find recognised by Bernard Fagg; Taruga excavated in January 1961; systematic fieldwork 2005-2021.

wiki-taruga.title: Taruga (Wikipedia)
wiki-taruga.author: Wikipedia contributors; cites Clark (Cambridge History of Africa vol. 2), Isichei 1997, Rupp, Breunig and Kahlheber 2008
wiki-taruga.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only.
wiki-taruga.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Location given only as about 60 km south-east of Abuja. Iron dates disagree: 'firmly dated' to 600 BC (Isichei) versus radiocarbon dates of about the 4th-3rd centuries BC (Fagg's excavation).

forumfed.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. 12 states in 1967 replacing four regions; seven more in 1976; FCT established in 1976 and the capital officially moved from Lagos in 1991; dates the Mid-Western Region to 1964 (most accounts give 1963).

thisday-1991.author: ThisDay
thisday-1991.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Osun, Edo, Kogi, Abia, Yobe, Delta, Jigawa, Kebbi and Taraba created on 27 August 1991 by Ibrahim Babangida.

dailytrust-1987.author: Daily Trust
dailytrust-1987.checked: Opened 26 Oct 2026. Katsina State created from the old Kaduna State on 23 September 1987 by Ibrahim Babangida.

wiki-trans-saharan.title: Trans-Saharan trade (Wikipedia)
wiki-trans-saharan.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-trans-saharan.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-trans-saharan.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-trans-saharan.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. From Kawar, caravans crossed the dunes of Bilma, where rock salt was mined, to the savanna north of Lake Chad; the shortest route, exchanging slaves and ivory from the south for salt; the Tripoli-Murzuk-Lake Chad road; regular routes only from the 7th and 8th centuries; the eastern route led to Kanem-Bornu.

wiki-kanem.title: Kanem Empire (Wikipedia)
wiki-kanem.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-kanem.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-kanem.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-kanem.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Core territory in Kanem, north-east of Lake Chad; the site of Njimi has never been located; founding typically dated to c. 700, with c. 600 and c. 900 also given; the Bilala took Njimi around 1380 and the court moved to Bornu; exported salt, ivory, slaves and animal products.

wiki-hausa.title: Hausa Kingdoms (Wikipedia)
wiki-hausa.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-hausa.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-hausa.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-hausa.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Daura the mother city; the Hausa Bakwai as seven states; fortified capital cities; by the 15th century trading centres competing with Kanem-Bornu and Mali; Bornu made the Hausa states vassals in the 15th century, tribute sent through Daura, unsure whether all or only Kano and Biram; Rano conquered by Kano under Yaji I; Tuareg and Fulani migration from the 14th and 15th centuries.

wiki-bornu.title: Bornu Empire (Wikipedia)
wiki-bornu.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-bornu.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-bornu.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-bornu.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Ngazargamu founded c. 1472 on the Yobe; captured and destroyed by the Fulani in 1808; mai Idris III recognised as suzerain of Kano and paid tribute.

wiki-fula.title: Fula people (Wikipedia)
wiki-fula.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-fula.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-fula.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-fula.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Origins unclear; Futa Toro supported by linguistic evidence; one estimate, mainly from oral tradition, has migrants leaving Futa Toro eastwards between the 11th and 14th centuries; a steady flow into Hausaland by the 15th century and later into Bornu; pastoral, semi-nomadic and settled Fulani.

wiki-benin.title: Kingdom of Benin (Wikipedia)
wiki-benin.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-benin.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-benin.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-benin.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Ewuare came to power in 1440 and expanded the former city-state; the capital was Edo, now Benin City; armies expanded west into eastern Yorubaland from the mid-15th century; influence reached Lagos by about the mid-1500s; the Niger appears to have been the effective eastern boundary of Benin rule.

wiki-benin-art.title: Benin court and ceremonial art (Wikipedia)
wiki-benin-art.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-benin-art.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-benin-art.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-benin-art.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. The leopard is one of the principal symbols of the Oba in Benin art; coral-bead regalia, mudfish and ivory trumpets also appear. The page gives no date for the leopard imagery.

wiki-aro.title: Aro Confederacy (Wikipedia)
wiki-aro.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-aro.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-aro.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-aro.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Origins in the mid-17th century (infobox 1640); Arochukwu as its centre with the Ibini Ukpabi oracle; traded with the Oguta, Onitsha and Kalabari monarchies; slave markets at Oguta Lake, Onitsha, Abonnema and Bonny; economy mainly enslaved people and palm oil; allies such as Ohafia, Edda and Abam; Arochukwu captured 28 Dec 1901, collapse by early 1902.

wiki-igbo.title: Igbo people (Wikipedia)
wiki-igbo.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-igbo.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-igbo.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-igbo.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Communities ruled by a republican consultative assembly and councils of elders; umunna patrilineages; the Ozo title society; Onitsha had kings called Obi; Nri and Arochukwu had priest-kings; warrant chiefs placed where there were no monarchies.

wiki-sokoto.title: Sokoto Caliphate (Wikipedia)
wiki-sokoto.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-sokoto.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-sokoto.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-sokoto.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Usman dan Fodio moved to Gudu in February 1804 and war was declared on 21 Feb 1804; Kano captured 1807; Sokoto founded by Muhammad Bello in 1809; Gwandu the western seat; emirs appointed by the caliph, with wide autonomy, pledged allegiance and brought tribute each year; the emirates recognised the Sultan of Sokoto's suzerainty; Attahiru I killed in June 1903 (text) or at Burmi on 27 Jul 1903 (infobox).

wiki-rnc.title: Royal Niger Company (Wikipedia)
wiki-rnc.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-rnc.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-rnc.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-rnc.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. On 1 Jan 1900 the company transferred its territories to the British government for £865,000; with the Niger Coast Protectorate they formed the Protectorates of Northern and Southern Nigeria.

wiki-battle-kano.title: Battle of Kano (Wikipedia)
wiki-battle-kano.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-battle-kano.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-battle-kano.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-battle-kano.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. A force under Colonel Thomas Morland left Zaria at the end of January 1903 and took Kano on 3 Feb 1903 after heavy fighting. Casualty figures conflict between the infobox and the text, so none are used.

wiki-battle-sokoto.title: Battle of Sokoto (Wikipedia)
wiki-battle-sokoto.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-battle-sokoto.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-battle-sokoto.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-battle-sokoto.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Battle fought on 15 Mar 1903 under Kemball and Morland; Attahiru I left the city and was killed at the Battle of Burmi in July 1903.

wiki-colonial-north.title: Colonial history of Northern Nigeria (Wikipedia)
wiki-colonial-north.author: Wikipedia contributors
wiki-colonial-north.kind: encyclopedia (secondary, used as a pointer to the works it cites)
wiki-colonial-north.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 text; facts cited only, no text reused.
wiki-colonial-north.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Kano's fort captured in February 1903, Sokoto shortly after; the caliphate's council conceded to Lugard's demands on 13 Mar 1903. The page also dates the proclamation of the protectorate to 1 Jan 1897 at Ida, which conflicts with other sources, so that is not used.

wiki-places-key.rights: Coordinates are facts; no text reused.
wiki-places-key.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026. Bilma 18.687 N 12.919 E; Mao (Kanem region, Chad) 14.119 N 15.313 E; Daura 13.036 N 8.318 E; Katsina 12.989 N 7.601 E (21 km city wall, founded c. 1100); Kano 12.000 N 8.517 E (walls begun under Gijimasu, 1095-1134); Ngazargamu ruins 13.083 N 12.367 E (near Geidam); Benin City 6.333 N 5.622 E; Arochukwu 5.383 N 7.917 E; Oguta 5.712 N 6.809 E (on Oguta Lake); Onitsha 6.167 N 6.783 E (founded 1630-1680, or the 16th century by some sources); Bonny 4.433 N 7.167 E (turned to palm oil after 1807); Sokoto 13.062 N 5.234 E (founded as a ribat in 1809); Gwandu 12.502 N 4.643 E (co-capital overseeing the western and southern lands); Zaria 11.067 N 7.700 E (captured by the Fulani in 1805, taken by British forces under Lugard in 1901).

fotw-rnc.title: Royal Niger Company (Flags of the World)
fotw-rnc.author: Flags of the World contributors
fotw-rnc.checked: Opened 27 Oct 2026 for the research outline. Badge: a black Y for the Niger and the Benue with ARS, JUS and PAX, in a red ring on white; on a White Ensign approved 2 Jun 1887, withdrawn 1 Feb 1888, then a Blue Ensign; use until 1899 presumed.

fotw-ng-gb.author: Flags of the World contributors
